text: @guowenzhang/dsh-mcp-manager 是面向 DSH Web 的 MCP 服务器管理插件。它在设置页提供服务器清单和编辑界面，并管理 MCP 服务器在会话中的加载方式。用户可以添加或编辑 stdio、HTTP 等服务器配置，按需加载服务器及工具，搜索和分页浏览工具目录，并通过工具规则筛选会话可用的工具。插件还保存发现过的工具目录，展示工具注释与估算上下文用量。适合需要管理多个 MCP 服务、控制工具上下文占用的 DSH 用户；需在 DSH 主机配置要连接的 MCP 服务。

@guowenzhang/dsh-mcp-manager adds MCP server management to DSH Web settings. It supports stdio and HTTP configurations, on-demand loading, tool search and paging, session filters, and a saved tool catalogue. Manage MCP services and control which tools enter a session.
想在 DSH 设置里统一添加和编辑 MCP 服务器配置。
希望 MCP 工具只在需要时加载，减少每次会话带入的工具信息。
需要搜索很多 MCP 服务器里的工具，并分批查看结果。
想限制某个会话能调用的 MCP 工具。
I want to manage MCP server connections from my DSH settings page.
Can I load MCP tools only when a session needs them?
@guowenzhang/dsh-mcp-manager 的功能「服务器配置」：在设置界面创建或编辑 MCP 服务器条目，支持 stdio 命令配置及 HTTP 类 URL 配置，并将其转换为 DSH MCP 客户端配置。
@guowenzhang/dsh-mcp-manager 的功能「按需加载 MCP 工具」：管理器协调 MCP 工具随会话加载，避免所有允许的服务器默认参与每次请求。
@guowenzhang/dsh-mcp-manager 的功能「搜索与分页工具目录」：提供工具查询、分页游标及列表优化逻辑，帮助从服务器目录中逐步发现工具。
@guowenzhang/dsh-mcp-manager 的功能「持久化工具目录」：缓存发现的 MCP 工具目录，并按连接配置区分记录；支持读取统计、失效和清空目录。
如何按服务器或工具规则缩小会话可用的 MCP 工具范围？
I need to find a particular tool across my configured MCP servers.

description: "Manage MCP servers in DeepSeek Harness, load them on demand, and filter tools to reduce context usage"
kind: "plugin-readme"
---

@guowenzhang/dsh-mcp-manager README · The problem this plugin solves：Adding MCP servers to DeepSeek Harness is inconvenient, and loading every configured server's tools by default consumes substantial context.

This plugin adds server creation, editing, and per-row switches to the settings page. With on-demand loading, the initial context contains only MCP names and descriptions; the model enables servers as needed during a session. Tool filtering lets you load only the tools you select.

@guowenzhang/dsh-mcp-manager README · The problem this plugin solves：In the plugin list, display names and descriptions follow the Harness language setting in English or Chinese (English is the default fallback); English names use the package name without its npm scope, Chinese names describe the purpose, and installation still uses the unchanged real package name.

@guowenzhang/dsh-mcp-manager README · Screenshots：One page with two tabs: **Servers** holds the roster, **Settings** holds the loading mode and how much of a tool list one call hands to the model. The server list scrolls independently while the page heading, tabs, Add button and filters stay in place. Agent preset names use the same Host translations as the new-session picker and update with the interface language; authored names remain unchanged. The roster is one list — global rows first, labelled **Global**, then the rows of the agent preset picked in the filter bar. Click the card itself to open the editor: **Config / Credentials / Tools**; a row that carries an environment or a header opens straight on **Credentials**. Where an added row is written is chosen in the dialog's own **Config scope** select, which lists the global plane and every declared agent preset in one field; the tools pane shows each tool's estimated token cost and the totals for what is loaded and what a rule would drop. A switch that fails reports in its own row with a retry.

@guowenzhang/dsh-mcp-manager README · Install：Requires DeepSeek Harness, `pnpm`, and Node.js ≥22.18 or ≥24.2.

```sh
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add @guowenzhang/dsh-mcp-manager@^1.1.0
```

@guowenzhang/dsh-mcp-manager README · Install：Restart the host and refresh the page, then open **Settings → MCP management** to add servers and describe their purpose. The page has two tabs: **Servers** (the roster: one list, global rows first with a **Global** label, then the rows of the agent preset the filter bar selects; click a card to open its editor, whose **Config / Credentials / Tools** panes hold the JSON, the environment or headers, and the tool list) and **Settings** (**MCP loading**, where Dynamic insert is the default, followed by how much of a tool list reaches the model). The **Config scope** select picks an added row's home in one field: the global plane, or one agent preset. In the add form the two fields marked `*` (server name, JSON configuration) are required, and the server name is filled from the JSON you paste (`npx -y @upstash/context7-mcp` → `context7`); once you edit it yourself, it is yours.
@guowenzhang/dsh-mcp-manager README · Install：See [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/zhang-guo-wen/dsh-mcp-manager/blob/master/AGENTS.md) for other installation methods and development instructions.

@guowenzhang/dsh-mcp-manager README · Reduce context further: search, paging, names only：**Settings → MCP management → Settings** controls how much of a tool list reaches the model, and carries the loading mode. The MCP specification has no query parameter on `tools/list` and no names-only listing, and the [client best-practices guide](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/2026-07-28/develop/clients/client-best-practices) places progressive discovery in the host — which is what this tab is:

text:
@guowenzhang/dsh-mcp-manager README · Reduce context further: search, paging, names only：| Setting | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Tool search** (`search`) | Registers `mcp_search`: the model finds tools by keyword across every discovered server and gets names plus one-line descriptions only. |
| **Index uncached servers** (`searchIndex`) | Lets a search connect to a server it has no tool list for (3 at a time, 8 seconds each). Off by default, so a search stays a cheap read. |
| **Items per listing** (`pageSize`) | `mcp_load` / `mcp_search` list at most this many items and return `nextCursor` for the rest. |
| **Names and descriptions only** (`namesOnly`) | `mcp_load` omits argument schemas by default; asking for one tool by name still returns that tool's full schema. |
| **Tools collected per server** (`maxTools`) | Caps the paginated `tools/list` walk, so an enormous server cannot flood a request. |
| **Show tool annotations** (`annotations`) | Carries the server's `readOnlyHint` / `destructiveHint` / `idempotentHint` / `openWorldHint` into listings. |
| **Hide destructive tools** (`hideDestructive`) | Keeps tools whose `destructiveHint` is explicitly true out of the session entirely. |

text: @guowenzhang/dsh-mcp-manager README · Reduce context further: search, paging, names only：**Tool catalogue database:** all MCP catalogues, including local `stdio` and HTTP/SSE/Streamable HTTP servers, persist in `<DSH_HOME>/cache/dsh-mcp-manager/<profile-hash>/catalog.sqlite`. Local directories remain until invalidated and are never connected by the Refresh button. HTTP servers that advertise `ttlMs` are rediscovered on the next search after expiry; without a TTL their directory remains until a manual refresh. Catalogue state sits directly below **Tool catalogue cache**. **Refresh** reconnects only currently enabled HTTP/SSE servers, retaining previous records and reporting individual failures; **Clear cache** removes all directories. There is no user-set cache lifetime. A successful add-form probe saves the directory immediately but does not save the MCP configuration; failed probes do not prevent direct saving. Configuration digests distinguish changed commands, arguments, effective cwd/environment, URLs and headers. The database stores public definitions and digests, not raw configuration or credentials; definitions themselves can contain server-provided sensitive text. Executing

@guowenzhang/dsh-mcp-manager README · Notes：- **On-demand loading covers both planes, and nothing starts at host start-up.** Under Dynamic insert (`dynamic`, default) and Lazy loading (`lazy`) an allowed row is suppressed before its plugin ever runs, so host start-up and Agent preset rebuilds start no MCP process at all; the first `mcp_load` starts the connection. Global composition rows follow the same loading mode: Load all (`eager`) mounts them from the composition, while `dynamic` / `lazy` keep them held until `mcp_load` starts one on a connection shared with other sessions. Tool filters still do not take effect on a global row.
- **Load on demand, then reuse.** Connections live in a host-level pool keyed by row and connection configuration: the same server loaded again — by the same session, another session, or a subagent — reuses that one connection (for stdio, the same child process). `mcp_unload` releases only the calling session's reference; the server stops when the last session releases it, and a session that ends releases its references.
